page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg9i.16xlarge is a dedicated compute-oriented virtual server instance belonging to the High Clock Speed instance family. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, it features 64 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor running at a base clock speed of 3.4 GHz. System memory is provisioned at 256.0 GB RAM, establishing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, necessitating the attachment of network-attached block storage for operating system images and persistent file systems. For inter-node communication and data ingestion, it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 36 Gbps. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs configured on this server, making graphics processing or GPU-accelerated computing workloads unsuitable.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of a high 3.4 GHz operating frequency and dedicated CPU allocation delivers stable compute capability per core without multi-tenant thread contention. Because it does not provision onboard NVMe storage, cost efficiency relies on properly matching external storage throughput with the 36 Gbps networking envelope, preventing I/O bottlenecks during distributed processing.

Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg9i.16xlarge is structured for workloads that require strong single-thread execution rates alongside wide parallelism across 64 cores. Typical target environments include enterprise relational database hosting, large-scale continuous integration and build pipelines, batch data processing, electronic design automation, and compute-heavy web serving layers.
